summary.prose: Building this Story first makes size refusals visible and never retried, gives providers a known input budget and adds a pure batch packer. On those it builds one serialisable review job in three stages (map, keyed reduce with capped merges, and quality's cross-part compare, with a fit-or-digest chain for any combined call), then gives each of the five symbol-reading dimensions its strategy and routes the judges through their jobs. The controller path then runs the same jobs one measured frame at a time, answered by call id through the MCP tool, and the Story ends by reviewing Epic c2ba6fa6 s1 on the installed daemon.

acceptanceChecks: codex input_too_large on any of its failure paths and a claude 'Prompt is too long' envelope each surface an InputTooLargeError from completeStructured after exactly one CLI run, with maxChars/actualChars when reported.
Error messages are unchanged; other errors are retried as today.

tasks.title: ReviewJob core: whole call, MAP, merge, refusals, daemon driver
tasks.summary: createReviewJob / nextCalls / applyAnswer with the whole-call path (one call with the supplied whole prompt when it fits or the budget is unknown), MAP over the cross product of each needed input source's batches (local findings and keyed notes, never absence findings), the finding merge (identical findings once) with parts counts, refusal re-planning (re-pack with the reported maxChars, else halves), and a daemon driver that runs a job's calls serially.
acceptanceChecks: A job whose whole prompt fits, or with an unknown budget, is exactly one call with the supplied whole prompt and schema.
Every MAP call fits when serialised and every original atom of every source is read whole by some MAP call, for inputs many times the budget.
A refused call is re-planned and no prompt is sent twice.

tasks.title: ReviewJob REDUCE: obligation keys, capped merge levels, context-only calls
tasks.summary: REDUCE keys initialised from every obligation before MAP; keys adjudicated in packed calls (a key with no notes too); a key whose notes do not fit is merged level by level into capped notes under short ids with provenance kept in the job; context-only calls when there are no symbols; merge answers over their cap or naming unknown note ids rejected.
acceptanceChecks: Every obligation reaches adjudication, including one with no notes and every one when there are no symbols.
A key whose symbolIds alone exceed the budget is merged under note ids, adjudicated in one call and its findings expanded to the real symbols; the job terminates.
A merge answer over its cap or naming unknown note ids is rejected.

tasks.title: ReviewJob COMPARE and the joint-fit chain
tasks.summary: COMPARE over pairs of description batches (each at most half the budget); the joint-fit chain (all full, one full with the others as digests, all digests) for every combining call, with digests capped at DIGEST_CHARS and written by calls that read their atom whole.
acceptanceChecks: Every pair of atoms in different description batches is compared by some call.
Two atoms that each fit alone but not together, including two near-budget atoms, are combined through the chain and every call fits when serialised.

tasks.title: Coverage strategy
tasks.summary: DimensionStrategy for coverage: test-record atoms (a file-status atom per file always, title atoms carrying file metadata, reported tests, BUILD task results, notes), MAP with only the reached files' atoms, REDUCE per promised test with its record atoms, context-only calls when there are no symbols, normalizeCoverageFindings once after the merge.
acceptanceChecks: With a test record larger than the budget, or no symbols, every promised test is adjudicated on all its evidence; a missing one is reported and a passing one is not.
A title-less failing or malformed test file keeps its state in every call naming it.

tasks.title: Controller jobs and emit_calls frames within the measured envelope
tasks.summary: The controller path keeps one ReviewJob per dimension in the step state; when the review does not fit today's single frame it emits next 'emit_calls' frames (calls with callId, dimension, stage, prompt, schema; no grounding or legacy prompts), planned with a per-call budget of controllerFrameChars minus the measured frame envelope and packed while the serialised frame fits. A review that fits one frame is exactly as today.
acceptanceChecks: Every serialised emit_calls frame fits controllerFrameChars, including a call near the frame budget.
A review that fits one frame produces today's emit_judgements frame unchanged.

tasks.title: Controller answers by callId, frame tokens and the MCP schema
tasks.summary: The judgements phase accepts answers [{ callId, output }] for an emit_calls frame; applyAnswer advances each job; a fresh token per frame with the previous released; a wrong callId is bad-judgements and a replayed token state-not-found; the insrc_code_review_step MCP input schema accepts answers, forwarded unchanged; the last answers drive the runner.
